title: AL Object ID Ninja: Self-Hosting vs. Hassle-Free (the data tells a curious story)
summary: AL Object ID Ninja, a tool for managing object IDs across teams, has distributed IDs to over 9,000 apps in three months. The post analyzes adoption data showing that while 3.2% of teams use private endpoints for self-hosting, only 1.3% configure them correctly for all team members, suggesting that the maintenance burden of self-hosting often exceeds the cost of a premium subscription.
key_points: AL Object ID Ninja has issued object IDs to 9,365 apps over three months
Only 297 apps (3.2%) configured private endpoints for self-hosting
Just 122 apps (1.3%) had fully reliable private endpoint setup across all team members
Self-hosting requires consistent discipline and synchronization, creating hidden maintenance costs

quotes.text: Only 122 apps were consistently configured correctly for all team members
quotes.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the practical difficulty of implementing self-hosted solutions reliably across teams
